outcome: Traetta's paper constructing solutions to the Oberwolfach problem OP(F) for every 2-regular graph F containing a cycle longer than an explicit lower bound was published in Discrete Mathematics in 2024, settling a genuine (non-asymptotic-in-n) case class of the exact problem as stated; the general problem, and the four known small exceptional non-instances, remain open. No AI involvement was found in any of the surveyed 2024-2026 work on this problem.
summary: The problem asks, for every 2-regular graph F on v vertices, whether K_v (v odd) or K_v minus a 1-factor (v even) decomposes into edge-disjoint copies of F. The 2021 Glock-Joos-Kim-Kuhn-Osthus result resolving this for all sufficiently large v (in terms of the number of vertices, for fixed cycle-structure type) predates the frozen revision (26 Jan 2024) and is already reflected in the Wikipedia statement's implicit context; it is not an in-window event. Within the window, the clearest genuine development is Tommaso Traetta's 'A constructive solution to the Oberwolfach problem with a large cycle.' The original preprint (arXiv:2306.12713v1) was posted 22 June 2023, before the window, and already contained the core construction: OP(F) is solved whenever F contains a cycle longer than an explicit lower bound (a case class defined by a structural property of F, not by v being asymptotically large -- this is a genuine restriction/case of the exact problem, not a variant, so it counts under the case-vs-variant test in DEEP_DIVE.md §3.1). However, a revised version (v2), reflecting acceptance for publication in Discrete Mathematics 347 (2024), art. 113947, was posted 13 February 2024 -- 18 days after the frozen revision's timestamp. Per §6.3, the first written argument is dated to v1 (June 2023), which would make this open_stale; but the expert-vetted, published form (the version on which the `resolved`/`partial` classification standard in §6.1 explicitly relies -- 'settled and digested by experts') only became available after the window opened, via v2 and the 2024 journal publication. I classified this as `partial` dated to v2 (13 Feb 2024) rather than `open_stale`, because the substantive published, peer-reviewed argument -- the version that counts as digested by experts under §6.1 -- did not exist until after 26 January 2024; the June 2023 preprint was an unrefereed claim at the time of the frozen revision. This is a judgment call and I flag it as such. Other 2024 work found by the triage (Lacaze-Masmonteil, 'Completing the solution of the directed Oberwolfach problem with cycles of equal length,' and a September 2024 arXiv paper on the two-table directed Oberwolfach problem) concerns the *directed* Oberwolfach problem, a distinct problem over the complete symmetric digraph rather than the complete graph K_v -- this is a related problem/variant under §3.1's test (it changes the object class, from undirected to directed graphs), not a case of the undirected problem stated in this Wikipedia bullet, so it does not count toward this record's status. I also checked the four known small exceptional instances where no decomposition exists (OP(3^2), OP(3^4), OP(4,5), OP(3,3,5)) and found no work resolving or revisiting them in the window. No source discussed here, or found in any search, mentions AI, machine learning, SAT solvers, or any automated system contributing to the mathematics; Traetta's construction is a purely human, combinatorial (amalgamation-detachment) argument. A search for AI angles on this specific problem (including a TechRadar story about a 'Chinese AI' solving a 'decade-old math problem') turned up a story about an unrelated commutative-algebra conjecture (Dan Anderson's 2014 conjecture, solved by a Rethlas/Archon dual-agent system from Peking University), confirming no AI connection to the Oberwolfach problem.
competing_reading: If the first written argument is dated strictly to v1 (22 June 2023, which already stated the full result and lower bound), then this event predates the frozen revision and the correct status is `open_stale` rather than `partial`, with the 2024 events (v2, journal publication) noted only as later confirmation/digestion of an already-existing claim. Under this reading, nothing that counts as a *new* result happened in the window at all, and the record would instead rest on `no_change_found` for the undirected problem specifically.
what_would_settle_it: Diffing arXiv v1 vs v2 of 2306.12713 to see whether v2 contains any new case, sharper bound, or corrected argument beyond copyediting for journal acceptance; if v2 is textually identical in substance to v1, the event should be redated to June 2023 and the status changed to open_stale.
